svg.text: lochness bench wiring (stage 1): parts on hand, one 830-point breadboard
Generated by build_wiring.py from wiring/bench.py. Same GPIO map as the dev kit, so the same firmware runs on both. Hole = row (1-63) + column (a-j) or rail.
Power: USB into the DevKit (its 3V3 and 5V feed the rails). 2x 18650 in series -> MP1584 (set to 6.0 V BEFORE connecting) -> TB6612 VM. All grounds common.
USB-C ports off the board's end
check the pin order on yours

Before powering: set the MP1584 to 6.0 V with a meter, unloaded. Charge each 18650 on its own with the TP4056 (it is a 1-cell charger), never the pair in series.
The pack has no protection: stop at 3.0 V per cell (6.0 V pack). If your rails are split halfway along, bridge each one across the split.
A3144: branded face towards you, legs 1 VCC, 2 GND, 3 OUT; needs a magnet's SOUTH pole on the branded face. Firmware: enable the pull-up on GPIO 22, 23 and 2.
TB6612 pin order is SparkFun's (ROB-14451); check your board's silkscreen. The DevKit is the DevKitC-1 (16 pins a side); a DevKitM-1 has the same GPIOs on other rows.
